CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SUBRAMONIUM PRASAD  OR % 12.09.2024 1.
The Petitioners seek bail in FIR No. 292/2018 dated 16.07.2018 registered at Police Station Mahendra Park for offences under Section 302, & 34 IPC.
Chargesheet has been filed for offences under Section 302, 120B, 420, 468, 471, 174A & 34 IPC read with Section 25, 27, 54 & 59 of the Arms Act.
2. The present FIR arises out of an incident that took place on 16.07.2017, resulting in death of one Rajesh Gupta.
There are 54 witnesses in total.
It is stated that chargesheet has been filed in September, 2018 and that out of 54 witnesses, only 4 witnesses have been examined.
3. The Petitioners are in custody for about four years.
It is stated that the examination of Rajender Gupta is fixed for 18.09.2024.
There are only three public witnesses who are left to be examined.
This Court is of the opinion that trial in this case is going woefully slow despite the directions dated 10.01.2024 passed in a bail application of a co-accused.
4. The three witnesses, i.e., Rajender Gupta, Vinit Jain and Sagar are This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2024 at 20:33:50 directed to be examined positively within a period of two months from today.
Let the examination of three witnesses be produced in Court on the next date of hearing.
7. The Investigating Officer is directed to ensure the presence of three witnesses in Court.
